title: Male borrowers who explicitly state their marital status may see faster funding.
Shorter pitch texts may predict faster funding for male borrowers.
Pitches from women that mention specific goals like college or certified seeds accelerate funding.
Pitches from women that emphasize personal traits like being hardworking or putting in hard work predict slower funding.
Pitches that provide concrete details about children or household stability accelerate funding for both men and women.
Pitches from women that use the term 'entrepreneur' to describe themselves tend to accelerate funding.
Pitches from women that specify the loan amount in the local currency tend to fund more slowly than those that do not.
Male borrowers who explicitly identify as single tend to fund more slowly than those who do not.
Pitches from women that explicitly state how many children they have tend to fund more slowly.
Mentioning the goal of expanding or developing the business may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning specific years of professional experience predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning environmental protection predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention dreams or future aspirations predict slower funding.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their age fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention children's education or food security fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their marital status fund more slowly.
